title: TikTok Selling Fees: Costs Explained
summary: Master TikTok selling fees with Reacher's guide. Understand all costs, commissions, and how to optimize your sales. Learn more today!
body_markdown:
## How to Choose tiktok selling fees


Choose a fee model by calculating the net contribution from each order, not by selecting the lowest percentage shown in a search result. Start with the product’s selling price, then record the category, seller discount, shipping charge, tax treatment, refund exposure, and payout timing. Next, separate TikTok’s referral deduction from payment processing, creator compensation, advertising, fulfillment, and product cost. This structure helps you identify the tiktok selling fees that apply to your catalog and prevents a high-GMV product from appearing more profitable than it is.


Confirm the active rate inside TikTok Shop Seller Center before publishing a product or changing its price. Published research reflects different policy periods: Printify and Darkroom commonly cite a 6% US referral fee for many categories, while other fee guides report 8% after policy or category changes. Darkroom also estimates payment processing at approximately 2.0%. These figures are planning references, not a universal schedule. Record the policy date, category rule, calculation base, and any promotional exception shown in your seller account.


### Separate platform charges from marketing costs


Build your worksheet with independent lines for referral commission, transaction or payment processing, affiliate commission, paid media, shipping subsidy, fulfillment, packaging, refunds, returns, and chargebacks. This distinction answers the question, “What is the TikTok Shop commission fee and transaction fee?” The first normally describes TikTok’s charge for facilitating a sale. The second refers to payment handling or order processing. A creator’s affiliate payout is neither charge. It is a marketing expense that you control through the commission rate and campaign terms.


Do not treat a creator percentage as a fixed platform requirement. Darkroom describes creator affiliate commissions commonly ranging from 5% to 20%, but that range is a third-party estimate and may vary by offer, creator, category, and campaign objective. Model the payout against the amount that actually qualifies for commission, then test profit after discounts and refunds. This approach also prevents confusion about the tiktok shop commission for creators, since creator compensation and TikTok’s own deduction affect the same order while serving different purposes.


### Test margin before scaling volume


Use three scenarios before committing inventory or ad spend: a full-price order, a discounted order with creator attribution, and a returned order. For every scenario, calculate revenue less platform deductions, affiliate payout, landed product cost, fulfillment, shipping, advertising, and expected refund loss. Keep tax and customer-paid shipping outside the product margin when your accounting treatment requires that separation. If a product only works under the full-price scenario, restrict discounts or adjust the offer before increasing traffic.


The[analytics dashboard](https://www.reacherapp.com/features/dashboard) is a useful featured tool for reviewing product demand, creator activity, sales signals, and category behavior before you allocate budget. Use those insights to identify promising products and partners, then validate every decision against settlement data. The FastMoss TikTok Data Analytics Platform does not replace Seller Center policy notices, order statements, or your accounting system. Reconcile actual deductions after each campaign and update your forecast whenever rates, refund rules, or payout terms change.
